parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no traveller-facing restriction: no criminalisation of gender expression, no facility or document rule, no entry screening, and no documented state hostility. Positive exposures are substantial — an anti-discrimination statute covering gender identity/expression in public establishments (directly service-relevant to a visitor), administrative gender recognition, partnership recognition, an equality ministry, an engaged civil society that secures retractions, and visible political acceptance. The deductions are enforcement-side: no formal bias-crime classification system, incomplete bias enforcement, microaggressions underreported out of fear, and harassment protocols that omit gender diversity. The bias counts lack denominators and are not scored. For an adult alone or with a minor, nothing documented produces custody, exclusion, or denial of care.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border, airline, hotel or ID-mismatch friction for trans visitors; no marker-mismatch or secondary-screening practice recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Administrative gender recognition (2022 law, in force Feb 2023) and long-standing partnership recognition signal institutional familiarity with diverse documents; resident-facing, climate only here.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry stage not covered by any source in the dossier; open question rather than documented harm.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Enforcement of the bias-crime framework is documented as incomplete, and no formal bias-incident classification system exists, weakening prosecution of identity-motivated offences.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Bias-motivated offences attract enhanced penalties; police do record 2-3 bias incidents monthly; no arrest, detention or custody practice targeting trans people is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any police encounter would run through a framework where recording exists but classification for hate-crime prosecution does not.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Small unitary state; the national anti-discrimination law (13/2019) applies uniformly to public establishments with no subnational variation recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No parent or higher-level restrictive regime applies; uniform national framework governs facilities and services.

care_services.exposure: New workplace harassment protocols criticised for omitting gender diversity and trans-specific harassment; no visitor-specific emergency-care or insurance practice documented.
care_services.protection: Law 13/2019 covers health care discrimination; October 2025 decree provides HRT via social security from 16 and surgery from 18 (resident-facing climate signal).
care_services.interaction: A traveller seeking care would enter a system whose statutory protections apply but whose operational protocols are acknowledged as gender-blind.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: A national newspaper published a transphobic column (Sept 2023); microaggressions are reported but rarely lodged with authorities, attributed to fear.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The column was removed with a public apology after advocacy complaint; equality ministry ran measures during the year; head of government publicly gay since 2023 and still in office.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing is affirming; the residual hostility is private media and everyday friction that demonstrably yields to complaint.

minors_guardians.exposure: Bullying and school discrimination documented for resident LGBT youth; parental expulsion reported; a 2000 murder case is dated and LGB-specific.
minors_guardians.protection: Law 14/2019 requires transgender children be respected in their gender identity; care coverage extends to under-16s via consultation.
minors_guardians.interaction: For a parent travelling with a minor, national law explicitly frames the child's identity as to be respected across education and services.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2-3 bias incidents monthly with no denominator, no motive breakdown and no classification system; advocacy groups report the prosecution gap. Underreporting due to fear suggests true levels are uncertain.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police maintain and publish bias-incident records; organised LGBT presence since 2002 with recurring Pride events; successful advocacy interventions.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recording exists but conversion to hate-crime prosecution is the documented weak link between street harm and remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No formal hate-crime registration and classification system; enforcement of bias provisions incomplete; no documented remedy outcome for a trans visitor.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Statutory anti-discrimination coverage across employment, education, health, housing and public establishments; equality ministry; civil society demonstrably effective at securing corrections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protections coexist with an acknowledged enforcement gap; remedies exist but their performance for visitors is untested in the record.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra operates a universal entry bar excluding transgender visitors with no remedy. This dossier documents no entry restriction, no registration, no exclusion and no state screening at all — an entirely different exposure tier. Nothing here is comparable to a border-integrity register.

Vellmaris shows a document-mismatch stop, intrusive questioning, and a complaint yielding apology and compensation but no officer discipline. This dossier records no traveller detention or stop whatsoever, alongside broader statutory coverage, so it sits clearly above this anchor.

Vessalia has equality law covering gender identity in public services, oversight investigating complaints, plus one rural officer stop and incomplete data. Very close: comparable statutory strength and comparable enforcement gaps, with this dossier lacking even the single documented officer incident.

Tarosven shows remedies actively working — investigations, licence withdrawal, published inspection findings. This dossier has strong law and social acceptance but no documented remedy performance for a visitor and an acknowledged hate-crime classification gap, so it sits a step below this enforcement-rich anchor.

parsed.synthesis: Law and society are aligned in acceptance: anti-discrimination statute covering gender identity/expression in public establishments reaches a visitor's hotels, clinics and venues; no criminalisation, no facility or document rule, no entry screening, and no state threat-framing exists in the record. Political and civil-society signals corroborate this (openly gay head of government, Pride since 2002, a transphobic column retracted with apology after complaint). The residual exposure is enforcement-side: no bias-crime classification system, incomplete bias enforcement, harassment protocols that omit gender diversity, and underreporting driven by fear. These are real but modest deductions from a genuinely protective regime. For an adult alone or with a minor, nothing documented produces custody, exclusion, denial of care, or official hostility; remaining unknowns are open questions, not exposures.
